title: Prepare variants for reference PCA

blocks.what_we_do: Identify common autosomal sites in the supplied reference subset and the cleaned study.
blocks.why: PCA should not be dominated by long stretches of correlated probes. The supplied reference was constructed from common, LD-pruned autosomal array sites, with an r^2 threshold of 0.15 in 200-kb windows and a 50,000-site cap. We intersect it with the study after QC rather than reintroduce sites that failed earlier checks. Study-specific PCs will be pruned again after defining the final cohort.
blocks.you_need: State 4.6; the reference subset supplied at 0.5.
blocks.command:
```{r s5-2}
reference <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "pca_reference", "ref1000g_grch38")
study_sites <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "4.6"), ".pvar"))
reference_sites <- guided_table(paste0(reference, ".pvar"))
common <- sort(intersect(study_sites$ID, reference_sites$ID))
guided_list(common, guided_path(cfg, "5.2", "common.txt"))
stopifnot(length(common) == 48614L)
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "5.2", guided_path(cfg, "5.2", "common.txt"), parent = "4.6")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
48,614 shared sites retained for reference PCA and projection.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and instructor reference counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Should sites excluded for variant QC be added back merely because they exist in the reference?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The reference comparison uses the retained study sites.

</details>
